questions.question: Raziya Sultan was the first and only female ruler of the Sultanate, who ascended the throne in:
questions.solution:
• Razia Sultana was the daughter of Ilutmish and served as the Sultan of Delhi from 1236 to 1240.
  • She was married to Malik Altunia, the governor of Bathinda.
  • She was buried in Kaithal, Haryana.
  • She was imprisoned by Malik Ikhtiyar-ud-din Altunia in the Qila Mubarak Fort (Bathinda).
  • The book Razia Queen of India was written by Rafiq Zakaria about her life.

questions.question: Which of the following Delhi sultans introduced two coins, namely silver tanka and copper jital?
questions.solution:
• Ilutmish (1210-1236) introduced the silver tanka and copper jital coins.
  • He was a slave and son-in-law of Qutbuddin Aibak.
  • He is considered the real founder of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question: Balban followed the tradition of 'Sijda and Pabos' from which of following traditions?
questions.solution:
• Balban followed the tradition of 'Sijda and Pabos' from the Persian tradition.
  • 'Sijda' refers to the act of prostration or bowing down.
  • 'Pabos' refers to the kissing of the monarch's feet.

questions.question: Who among the following Delhi Sultanate rulers took the policy of 'blood and iron' to deal with the Mewati community?
questions.solution:
• The policy of 'blood and iron' implied being ruthless to enemies, using the sword, harshness, and shedding blood.
  • Ghiyas ud din Balban was the ninth sultan of the Mamluk/Slave dynasty of Delhi.
  • He adopted this policy to deal with the Mewati community.

questions.question: Mameluke style of architecture belongs to which dynasty?
questions.solution:
• The Slave dynasty (1206-1290) is also known as the Mamluk Dynasty.
  • It was established by Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-1210).
  • Capitals: Lahore and Delhi.
  • Famous buildings built by rulers of the slave dynasty:
    • Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque
    • Qutub Minar
    • Adhai Din ka Jhonpra
    • Tomb of Nasir-ud-Din Mohammed
    • Tomb of Shams-ud-Din Ilutmish

questions.question: The Delhi sultan, who succumbed to injuries as a result of his fall from horse, was
questions.solution:
• Qutbuddin Aibak (known as Lakh Baksh) was the slave of Muhammad Ghori and the first sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
  • He established the Slave dynasty (Mamluk dynasty).
  • He died after falling from a horse in Lahore, Pakistan.
  • Famous rulers of Slave Dynasty (1206 AD - 1290 AD): Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-1210), Shamsuddin Ilutmish (1210-1236), Raziya Sultan (1236-1240), Balban (1266-1287).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Ilutmish:
Statement 1: The Tomb of Ilutmish was built in 1388 AD.
Statement 2: Ilutmish introduced the gold coin 'Mohur' as the standard currency of the Delhi Sultanate.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: Ilutmish's tomb was built in 1235 AD, not 1388 AD.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: He introduced Tanka (silver) and Jital (copper), not the gold Mohur.

questions.question: Who started the practice of celebrating Nauroz during the Delhi Sultanate period?
questions.solution:
• Ghiyasaddin Balban started the practice of celebrating Nauroz.
  • Nowruz is the Iranian New Year, also known as the Persian New Year.

questions.question:
Statement 1: Balban served as Naib (Deputy) to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud.
Statement 2: Balban served as Naib to Sultan Razia.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Balban served as Naib (Deputy) to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud (1246-1266 AD), the eighth ruler of the Slave dynasty.
  • During this period, Balban gained administrative and military experience, which later helped him become Sultan in 1266 AD.
  • Razia Sultan (1236-1240 AD) was the first Muslim woman ruler, but Balban never served as her Naib.

questions.question: Who among the following revolted against Balban, Sultan of Delhi, and declared himself as an independent ruler of Bengal in 1279?
questions.solution:
• Tughril Beg revolted against Balban and declared himself independent ruler of Bengal in 1279.
  • Balban (Mamluk/Slave Dynasty) appointed his own son Bughra Khan as governor of Bengal after suppressing the revolt.
  • Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq was the last sultan of the Tughlaq dynasty.

questions.question: Who occupied Baduan (A.D. 1197-98) and appointed Ilutmish as its first Muslim Governor?
questions.solution:
• Qutbuddin Aibak (1206-1210), the first ruler of the Slave Dynasty/Mamluk Dynasty, occupied Baduan.
  • He appointed Ilutmish as its first Muslim Governor.
  • He was also known as Lakh Baksh.
  • He died in Lahore, Pakistan after falling from a horse.

questions.question: Qutb Minar is an example of ______ architecture.
questions.solution:
• Qutb Minar is an example of Indo-Islamic architecture.
  • Indo-Islamic architecture is the architecture of the Indian subcontinent produced for Islamic patrons and purposes.
  • Famous examples: City of Mandu (Madhya Pradesh), Taj Mahal (Agra), Gol Gumbaz (Karnataka), Jama Masjid (Delhi).

questions.question: What is the approximate height (in metres) of the Qutb Minar situated in Delhi?
questions.solution:
• The approximate height of Qutb Minar is 73 metres (239.5 ft approx).
  • Qutb Minar has five storeys.
  • It was started in 1199 by Qutb-ud-Din Aibak and completed in 1220 by his son-in-law Ilutmish.
  • UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1993.
  • Other important Minars: Charminar, Hyderabad (1591) by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, height 48.7 m (160 ft).

questions.question:
Statement 1: Nizam ul-Mulk Junaidi was the Wazir of Sultan Ilutmish.
Statement 2: Nusrat Khan was appointed as the Wazir of Ilutmish.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Sultan Ilutmish (1210-1236 AD) appointed Nizam ul-Mulk Junaidi as his Wazir.
  • He played an important role in administration and strengthening the Delhi Sultanate.
  • Nusrat Khan was not associated with Ilutmish as Wazir.

questions.question: Ghiyasuddin Balban, ruler of the Slave dynasty, took up the title of
questions.solution:
• Ghiyasuddin Balban took the title 'Zil-il-Ilahi' (shadow of God).
  • He abolished the Chahalghani (Council of 40 nobles).
  • He introduced Persian customs like Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the feet of the sultan).
  • He established Diwan-i-Ariz (defence department).

questions.question: In which of the following forts was Razia Sultan imprisoned by Malik Ikhtiyar-ud-din Altunia?
questions.solution:
• Razia Sultan was imprisoned in Qila Mubarak in Bathinda, built by Raja Dab.
  • Jaigarh fort in Jaipur was built in 1726 AD by Jai Singh II.
  • Golconda fort was built by the Qutb Shahi dynasty.
  • Mehrangarh fort in Jodhpur was built by Rao Jodha.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the market reforms of Delhi Sultans:
1. Alauddin Khalji set up three separate markets in Delhi for grain, cloth, and horses/slaves/cattle.
2. The market superintendent appointed by Alauddin Khalji was called Diwan-i-Arz.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Alauddin Khalji introduced strict market control and established three separate markets in Delhi for grain, cloth, and horses/slaves/cattle.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: He appointed a market superintendent called Shahna-i-Mandi, not Diwan-i-Arz (which was the military department created by Balban).

questions.question: The first southern campaign of Alauddin Khilji in 1307-08 AD was led to which of the following regions?
questions.solution:
• The first southern campaign of Alauddin Khilji in 1307-08 AD was led to Devagiri (modern-day Daulatabad, Maharashtra).
  • This campaign marked the beginning of the Delhi Sultanate's expansion into southern India.
  • Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316) also captured Ranthambore (1301), Chittor (1303), Malwa (1305), Madurai (1311), and Dwarasamudra (1310-11).

questions.question: Who amongst the following Delhi Sultanate rulers sent his army under Malik Kafur's command to conquer South India?
questions.solution:
• Alauddin Khilji sent his army under Malik Kafur's command to conquer South India.
  • Malik Kafur, also known as 'Hazar Dinar', was a slave of Ala-ud-din Khilji.
  • He led the army in the battle against Ramachandra of Devagiri.
  • Administrative reforms: implemented 'dagh Pratha' (branding horses) and 'Huliya Pratha' (system of ranks).

questions.question: Which of the following Sultans of Delhi set up the officers like Barid (intelligence officer) and Munhiyans (secret spies) to control the market?
questions.solution:
• Alauddin Khilji set up officers like Barid (intelligence officer) and Munhiyans (secret spies) to control the market.
  • He is known for implementing significant market reforms and establishing strict price controls.

questions.question: Who among the following Sultans framed a series of regulations to weaken the power of nobles?
questions.solution:
• Alauddin Khilji (Khilji Dynasty 1290-1320) framed regulations to weaken the power of nobles.
  • He made nobles pay land tax for their holdings, curbing their excess wealth.
  • Nobles were ordered not to have social gatherings or intermarriages without his permission.
  • He curbed the power of the group of nobles called 'The Forty'.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Amir Khusrau:
1. He was known as Tuti-e-Hind and was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya.
2. He popularized Qawwali, a form of music derived from the Arabic word qaul.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Both statements are correct.
  • Amir Khusrau, a celebrated poet and musician of the Sultanate period, was called Tuti-e-Hind (Parrot of India).
  • He was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya.
  • He is credited with popularizing Qawwali, a form of music derived from the Arabic word 'qaul' (saying).

questions.question: Which of the following Sultans of Delhi was appointed as Amir-i-Tuzuk (Master of Ceremonies) before becoming the Sultan?
questions.solution:
• Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316) was appointed as Amir-i-Tuzuk (Master of Ceremonies) before becoming Sultan.
  • He was the second ruler of the Khilji dynasty after Jalaluddin Khilji (founder of Khalji Dynasty).
  • He was also appointed Arizi-i-Mumalik (Minister of War) during Jalaluddin Khilji's reign.
  • He laid the foundation of his capital Siri in 1303 AD.

questions.question: Who was the first to mention the incident of Jauhar in Persian?
questions.solution:
• Amir Khusrau was the first to mention the incident of Jauhar in Persian.
  • 'Jauhar' refers to the collective self-immolation by women to escape capture and forced slavery by invaders in the face of imminent defeat.

questions.question: During Alauddin Khilji's reign, the cloth market was known as
questions.solution:
• During Alauddin Khilji's reign, the cloth market was known as Sarai-i-Adl (Place of Justice).
  • Alauddin Khilji built three markets for foodgrain, precious clothes, and slave/cattle near Kushke Sabz (Hara Rajmahal) within the Baduan gate in Delhi.
  • These were government-aided markets.
